lines: Routine follow-up visit for recently diagnosed essential hypertension with medication side effects

He denies chest pain, palpitations, or weight changes.

lines: Wife expresses concern about deteriorating financial situation and patient's recent secretive behavior
The patient is a 44-year-old male with essential hypertension, hyperlipidemia, HIV infection, and coronary artery disease who returns for follow-up evaluation of his gambling behaviors.
He admits to spending significant amounts of time at a local casino, often lying about his whereabouts.
He reports that he feels a constant urge to gamble, and despite recent substantial financial losses, he believes he can win back the money.
He has taken multiple loans and maxed out several credit cards.
The patient's medical history is notable for hypertension.

encounters.cc: Follow-up visit four months after HIV diagnosis with body habitus changes

lines: Follow-up visit four months after HIV diagnosis with body habitus changes

The patient is a 44-year-old male with essential hypertension, hyperlipidemia, coronary artery disease, and HIV infection diagnosed four months prior, returning for follow-up evaluation of body habitus changes.
He was recently seen in Psychiatry for pathological gambling and has a history of hydrochlorothiazide adverse reaction.
He reports that since starting his new medication regimen, he has noticed significant changes in his body.
He says his face has become rounder, and he has gained fat in his upper back while losing fat in his arms and legs.
He also mentions that his clothes no longer fit properly, and he feels self-conscious about the redistribution of body fat.
He has also been more fatigued and sometimes feels unusually thirsty.
He has no history of opportunistic infections, and he has been compliant with his therapy.
His other past medical history is notable only for well-controlled hypertension.
- Percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement (prior inferior STEMI)
- Conservative management of left-sided rib fractures
- Father: premature myocardial infarction at age 55
He works as an accountant and does not use alcohol, tobacco, or illicit drugs.
He is in a stable relationship and practices safe sex.
On exam, he is afebrile, and his vital signs are normal.
He has a rounded "moon face" and fat accumulation over the posterior neck.
His extremities appear thinner compared to central areas.
Cardiovascular and pulmonary exams are normal.
Neurological exam is intact with no focal deficits.
Laboratory workup from his last visit noted elevated fasting glucose.

encounters.cc: Intermittent chest pain occurring with exertion and resolving with rest

lines: Intermittent chest pain occurring with exertion and resolving with rest
Patient with coronary artery disease and HIV infection returns.
He reports pain that occurs during exercise and resolves with rest.
- Percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement (prior inferior STEMI)
- Conservative management of left-sided rib fractures
No family history of coronary artery disease
Blood pressure of 135/85 mmHg, heart rate of 78 bpm
Subsequent cardiac catheterization shows a 70% stenosis of the left anterior descending artery
An exercise stress test is performed, and the patient develops chest pain and ST-segment depression at a high level of exertion
The patient is enrolled in a clinical trial comparing a new anti-anginal medication to placebo.
After 6 months, the trial results show a p-value of 0.03 when comparing the frequency of angina episodes between the new medication and placebo groups.
The significance level α was set at 5% prior to the study.

lines: Sudden onset of severe chest pain radiating to left arm while mowing lawn

- Percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement (prior inferior STEMI)
